description: Understanding pacemaker function and ECG patterns
overview: This module covers pacemaker basics, different pacing modes, and ECG recognition of pacemaker rhythms.

slides.title: Pacemaker Basics
slides.content: Pacemakers are electronic devices that provide electrical stimulation to maintain heart rhythm. Components include generator, leads, and electrodes.

slides.title: Pacing Modes
slides.content: Common pacing modes: VVI (ventricular demand), DDD (dual chamber), AAI (atrial demand). Each mode has specific indications and ECG patterns.

quiz.question: What does VVI pacing mode mean?
quiz.explanation: VVI means ventricular demand pacing with ventricular sensing and inhibition.

slides.title: Pacemaker ECG Patterns
slides.content: Pacemaker spikes appear as vertical lines before paced beats. Atrial pacing shows spikes before P waves, ventricular pacing shows spikes before QRS complexes.

quiz.question: What appears as vertical lines before paced beats?
quiz.explanation: Pacemaker spikes appear as vertical lines before paced beats on the ECG.

slides.title: Pacemaker Malfunction
slides.content: Common malfunctions: failure to capture, failure to sense, oversensing, undersensing. Recognition and troubleshooting are essential for patient safety.

quiz.question: What indicates pacemaker failure to capture?
quiz.explanation: Failure to capture is indicated by pacemaker spikes without subsequent QRS response.
